extracted.intended_audience: Biomedical researchers (faculty-level) at U.S. research institutions who might apply to the HHMI Investigator Program or participate in HHMI programs
extracted.subtask_description: Description of the HHMI Investigator Program selection philosophy, eligibility, appointment terms, and program-specific award criteria (including Collaborative Innovation Awards and HHMI–GBMF plant investigator support). Emphasizes selecting individuals, risk-taking, interdisciplinarity, and potential for transformative contributions to biomedical science.

rubrics_metrics.name: People, not projects (selection philosophy)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI's philosophy of selecting 'people, not projects' — seeks researchers who bring innovative approaches to the study of many different biological problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection focuses on individuals' creativity, productivity, and potential to make significant contributions. HHMI provides long-term, flexible support (salary, benefits, research budget) to enable investigators to pursue their ideas over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to take risks and embrace failure
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI urges its researchers to take risks, explore unproven avenues, and embrace the unknown — even if it means uncertainty or the chance of failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate a record or potential for pursuing high-risk/high-reward research; HHMI tolerates and funds exploratory, uncertain lines of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue significant biological questions with rigor and depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators identify and pursue significant biological questions in a rigorous and deep manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated ability to define important biological problems and pursue them with thorough, rigorous experimental or conceptual approaches is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop new tools and methods to enable creative experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators 'develop new tools and methods that enable creative experimental approaches to biological questions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for researchers who create new methodologies or technologies that open up novel experimental directions or make previously intractable questions addressable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary approaches and bringing in other disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: When necessary, investigators bring to bear concepts or techniques from other disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-disciplinary integration (e.g., biophysics, engineering, computational approaches) that enhances biological insight is explicitly encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forge links between basic biology and medicine (translational potential)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators 'forge links between basic biology and medicine, opening new pathways for disease diagnosis and drug discovery.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that connects fundamental biological mechanisms to medical applications or new avenues for diagnosis/therapy is favorably regarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of eligible disciplines (inclusivity of fields)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI seeks researchers across many biomedical disciplines and adjacent fields — genetics, cell biology, developmental biology, biochemistry, neuroscience, biophysics, chemical biology, biomedical engineering, computational biology, plant sciences, experimental evolutionary biology, and patient-oriented research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants from diverse areas of the life sciences (including underfunded areas like plant biology and interdisciplinary domains) are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term flexible funding and employment arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI employs investigators (rather than awarding project grants), providing full salary, benefits, and a research budget, enabling freedom to explore and change direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The funding model is designed to give investigators freedom to follow ideas over long timeframes without tying support to a single specific project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment term and renewal: five-year term with exacting review
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are appointed for a five-year term, which may be renewed after an exacting review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal is conditional on a rigorous evaluation of progress and potential; applicants should expect periodic high-standard reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and application process (periodic competitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI accepts applications through periodic competitions from researchers at more than 200 research institutions across the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are solicited during periodic competitions; potential applicants should watch program announcements (the page notes 'There is no competition at this time').

rubrics_metrics.name: HHMI–GBMF plant investigator support (criteria for plant scientists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Through a partnership with the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation, HHMI appoints plant biologists as investigators to support creative plant scientists pursuing bold research with potential for large contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This track prioritizes creative plant biology research, addressing historical underfunding in plant sciences; supported projects are expected to be bold and impactful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative Innovation Awards (HCIA) — interdisciplinary team and transformative scope
rubrics_metrics.description: HCIA support interdisciplinary teams (each headed by an HHMI investigator) pursuing potentially transformative research projects that are new and so large in scope they require a team with a range of expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HCIA-funded projects should be collaborative (inside and outside HHMI), interdisciplinary, high-risk/high-reward, and large in scope; each collaborator receives funds for their research budget over four years and flexibility to pursue their ideas. HCIA awards are made after inviting HHMI investigators to propose collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for continued engagement with host institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators continue to be based at and participate in educational and administrative activities at their host institutions while receiving HHMI support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be prepared to maintain active roles at their home institutions (teaching/administration) alongside HHMI-supported research; host-institution partnerships are part of the arrangement.
